text:
maria_s: quick heads-up — customer compliance run flagged gaps in audit coverage for a couple of cross-tenant actions (token rotations, ingest-rekey, and delegation changes). can we map what's missing vs. schema we plan to ship?

tarek_dev: can you list the exact actions? is this about missing fields or missing event emission entirely? :thinking_face:

maria_s: both. e.g. when we rotate tenant KMS keys we emit audit.event.type=key.rotate but payload lacks tenant_id in some paths (old code path in shipper). also delegation grant/revoke has inconsistent actor.identity. customers want deterministic fields for downstream SIEM.

jenna_ops: we also see the high-volume path (hot ingest) coalescing some audit events into a single batch that loses the original request_id. that's what support flagged — they can't tie the event back to an operation.

sam_ir: this matters for incident response. request_id + tenant_id + action must be present and indexed for 30d. personally prefer explicit fields rather than embedded json blob for easier indexing.

alex_plat: architecturally we can add canonical fields: tenant_id, request_id, actor_id, event_type, resource_id, outcome, timestamp_iso. payload stays as raw_event for full context. schema bump v2.1 then migration plan for existing events.

maria_s: ok. two operational risks: 1) adding these fields increases index size and cost (esp for high-volume customers) and 2) the hotpath currently drops request_id for throughput reasons. need tradeoffs and a customer-facing validation plan.

tarek_dev: proposal: emit canonical fields always, but allow per-tenant sampling/field-drop policy controlled by RBAC/contract. default: full fields for enterprise + compliance customers, sampled/minimal for free tier. RBAC change needed to allow tenants to opt into full audit TTL and indexing.

jenna_ops: how do we enforce KMS integration here? If tenant_key rotation triggers an audit, we must ensure the event is signed and that logs reference the KMS key id but not leak key material. kms-bot: "Notice: rotation events will include kms_key_id but not key material. audit events are signed with tenant_proof signature v1."

sam_ir: from IR perspective that's fine. need assurance that signing proof contains stable fields to allow verification later. add proof.signature and proof.algorithm as canonical fields.

alex_plat: on cost/backpressure: our current ES write pipeline at 100k/sec with 7 fields added increases daily index by ~18% in our test. ballpark cost impact ~$1.8k/day for that workload. if we add request_id and tenant_id as keywords (not analyzed) cost is mostly shards + indexing ops.

maria_s: can we compress by storing request_id in a hot KV cache for 7 days and only index it on demand? customer compliance requires searchable fields — they expect SIEM-friendly index. some customers will pay, others won't.

tarek_dev: alternatives: 1) tiered retention: canonical indexed fields for 30d for paid customers, aggregated-only or hashed IDs for others; 2) use prefix compression on ES + doc-values; 3) switch heavy customers to a dedicated time-series store with cheaper index costs.

jenna_ops: we also need to handle ingestion backpressure: propose adding a circuit-breaker that returns 429 for best-effort tenants when write queue > 80% and falls back to event sampling with a sampled_count metric included. must include customer-facing messaging in status page and docs.

sam_ir: add a validation contract for customers: https://redwood.internal/audit-contracts — each audit event must include the canonical set or the tenant must opt-in to reduced coverage. For incident playbooks, we only run full for tenants with full coverage.

maria_s: next steps: (1) tally exact missing fields across release branches — @tarek_dev can you run a quick grep + unit test patch to assert canonical fields? (2) cost model for three scenarios — @alex_plat to produce per-1M-events cost delta with index-sizing; (3) RBAC toggle design doc for tenant opt-ins — @jenna_ops to draft; (4) customer-facing validation and migration notes — I'll draft with sam_ir for IR constraints.

tarek_dev: on it. I'll open a tiny PR with tests and a short benchmark script that emits v2.1 vs v2.0 payloads and computes index delta. expect PR today.

alex_plat: I'll run a perf job on staging cluster with a representative 150k qps burst to model backpressure and 95th p90 indexing latency. will share numbers.

jenna_ops: I'll sketch the RBAC toggle: admin role controls audit_tier {minimal, standard, full}, enforceable via policy checks in the control plane; needs clarity on billing consequences.

sam_ir: I'll prepare customer FAQ and migration checklist for customers who need guaranteed coverage for audits. also add recommended log retention/archiving for 1yr cold storage if they require it.

maria_s: thanks. one more: add an automated validator that runs on deploy to ensure no code path emits event without tenant_id/request_id — fail CI for security-critical paths. that should reduce regressions.

tarek_dev: agreed. I'll add a small linter rule and a runtime check in the shipper.

maria_s: perfect. if anyone wants to join the PR review ping me. closing loop in a few hours with the checklist. :lock:
